newsitem.title: USA: Ex-energy secretary sees nuclear disposal approved.
newsitem.headline: Ex-energy secretary sees nuclear disposal approved.

text.p: Former Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary said Wednesday she expects the government will clear the way to establish a place to store spent nuclear waste in Nevada.
"They will license that repository," she told a press conference in which she looked back at her four stormy years running the Energy Department which overseas the production of nuclear weapons.
She blamed "the junior staffers at the White House" for lacking the technical knowledge to help reach decisions on the controversial plan to store nuclear waste.
"This is not a political issue," she said. "This is an economic and national security issue."
The nuclear power industry, joined by 33 states where nuclear reactors are located, have asked a federal appeals court to force the federal government to dispose of the waste.
The Energy Department has been conducting feasibility studies for an underground site in Yucca Mountain in Nevada, about 100 miles from Las Vegas.
O'Leary said a key test, drilling a five-mile hole through the mountain, should be finished this Spring, clearing the way for a decision on the storage facility.

She also said the only way to lower U.S. dependence on foreign oil imports was to develop alternative fuels, but she said that attempts to provide tax and development incentives are politically difficult because "it would be characterised as corporate welfare."
O'Leary said that real efforts to develop alternatives would not be discussed "unless there is a crisis."
She said that the United States should encourage oil and gas development in the Caspian Sea as an alternative source to the Middle East.
